nodes.t: AI turns math into machine-checked proofs at scale
nodes.d: Agents turn informal proofs into Lean and complete them, at the scale of hundreds of papers or a multi-million-line project in weeks.

nodes.t: Research-grade math inside the labs
nodes.d: Frontier labs' internal models resolve research-level open problems on request, across all of mathematics, at about three hours of compute per result, with agent-written Lean for a large minority of results.

nodes.t: Independent checks of AI math
nodes.d: Outside groups run Comparator on the labs' Lean challenges and audit formal statements against the manuscripts, moving key results from T3 to T4.

nodes.t: AI does research-grade applied math
nodes.d: Engineers routinely get, from AI, well-posedness and stability analyses of their own models, numerical schemes with certified error bounds, uncertainty quantification with guarantees, and optimal-control results with proofs, for low-dimensional and reduced models…

nodes.t: Research-grade math for outside teams
nodes.d: An outside engineering team can buy, on demand, mathematics at roughly the October-2026 internal level (journal-grade open problems, proofs with Lean output) through a public or trusted-access product, for under ~$1,000 per result.

nodes.t: A research result costs less than an engineer-day
nodes.d: The public price of a research-grade math result (problem posed to checked proof or derivation) falls below ~$1,000 and then below ~$100, cheaper than one day of a specialist's time.

nodes.t: Published error rate for openai/math results
nodes.d: An independent expert team audits a random sample of 30 or more openai/math families (formalized and unformalized), checking statements against manuscripts and proofs or Comparator runs, and publishes an error and scope-gap rate.

nodes.t: AI-run closed-loop labs at scale
nodes.d: AI plans, runs and interprets experiments on robotic lab hardware, closing design-build-test loops for materials, chemistry and components at 10x or more the throughput of human-run labs.

nodes.t: AI multiphysics design with guarantees
nodes.d: AI runs end-to-end multiphysics design optimization (aero-thermal-structural-propulsion) with constraint satisfaction and model-relative error bounds inside validated envelopes (physical margins still come from test), producing designs that pass existing engineering review gates.

nodes.t: Frontier math on export-controlled and classified networks
nodes.d: Research-grade models run inside ITAR/EAR-compliant, CUI and classified environments, so space primes, Space Force and NRO programs can pose problems with export-controlled engineering data.

nodes.t: Month-long autonomous research tasks
nodes.d: AI agents complete, at 50% reliability or better, technical research tasks that take a human expert a full work-month (~170 hours), up from about a work-week in late 2026.

nodes.t: Open-weight model at research-math level
nodes.d: An open-weight model matches the October-2026 internal research-math level, removing lab release decisions and access controls as a gate for everyone, including adversaries.

nodes.t: Lean libraries for the math engineers use
nodes.d: Mathlib or companion libraries cover Sobolev spaces, weak solutions, standard PDE energy estimates, ODE and numerical-analysis theory, and stochastic processes well enough that applied results formalize routinely.

nodes.t: Verified floating-point and numerics toolchain
nodes.d: A toolchain that proves floating-point programs and numerical methods (ODE integrators, linear solvers, convex optimizers, filters) meet stated error bounds, from the mathematics down to compiled code.

nodes.t: AI builds validated physics theory
nodes.d: AI derives closures, reduced-order models with proofs, and plasma, materials or combustion theory that beat the human state of the art on held-out experimental data.

nodes.t: AI speeds up its own development 3x
nodes.d: AI systems accelerate frontier AI research and engineering, including chip design and software stacks, by 3x or more overall - the hinge between the base case and Recursive.

nodes.t: AI-discovered algorithms in space codes
nodes.d: AlphaEvolve-style search (a model proposes code, an automatic evaluator scores it) improves practical heuristics and kernels used in space operations and engineering: constellation scheduling, conjunction screening, trajectory solvers, onboard compression, CFD kernels.

nodes.t: AI results audited and trusted in days
nodes.d: AI-assisted pipelines check that a formal statement matches the engineering claim (definitions, hypotheses, units, scope), cross-check proofs with independent agents and produce human-readable audit trails, cutting the cost of trusting an AI result from expert-weeks to days.

nodes.t: AI emulators of space physics codes with stated error bounds
nodes.d: The weather-model playbook - train on decades of simulation or reanalysis data, run ~1,000x cheaper - applied to space codes (CFD and aerothermal, plasma, thermosphere, structures), with calibrated uncertainty or error bounds relative to the parent code…

nodes.t: On-demand applied math in space engineering
nodes.d: Space engineering organizations routinely pose their own hard analysis problems (stability, bounds, convergence, inverse problems, trade studies) to frontier models and use the checked answers in design reviews.

nodes.t: Both Starship stages caught and reflown
nodes.d: A Starship V3 booster and ship are each recovered and flown again, the threshold that turns a $200-250M expendable stack into an amortizable fleet.

nodes.t: Monthly flight testing of a fully reusable heavy launcher
nodes.d: A new fully reusable heavy launcher (Starship V3) flies at least 12 integrated flights in one calendar year, so flight data rather than analysis sets the pace of learning.

nodes.t: Reflight cleared by data, not teardown
nodes.d: Reusable stages are cleared for reflight from flight sensor data and a probabilistic life model (a digital twin) instead of detailed inspection, enabling booster turnaround under a week and ship turnaround under two weeks.

nodes.t: Spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
nodes.d: An operational spacecraft whose design analyses, trade studies and flight-software verification artifacts were majority AI-generated (with human review) reaches orbit and operates.

nodes.t: Pads and propellant plants for hundreds of heavy flights
nodes.d: At least four Starship-capable pads operate (Starbase pads 1 and 2, LC-39A, SLC-37 or equivalent) with on-site or pipeline propellant supply, removing pad count and cryogen trucking as cadence limits.

nodes.t: 100+ fully reusable heavy launches a year
nodes.d: Fully reusable heavy launchers fly 100 or more orbital missions in one calendar year.

nodes.t: A second reusable heavy-lift fleet at scale
nodes.d: A non-SpaceX reusable medium or heavy launcher fleet (New Glenn, Neutron, Terran R, Long March 10B, Zhuque-3 or another) flies 20 or more missions with reflown boosters in one calendar year.

nodes.t: Crew and defense payloads fly on data-cleared reused rockets
nodes.d: NASA crew or NASA Category 3 payloads, or NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 missions, fly on reflown Starship-class hardware whose reflight clearance rests largely on flight data and life models rather than teardown inspection.

nodes.t: A launcher or large spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
nodes.d: A launch-vehicle stage, a crew or cargo vehicle, or a non-constellation spacecraft over 5 t dry mass, whose design analyses, trades and verification artifacts were mostly AI-generated (with human review), flies and operates.

nodes.t: 300+ fully reusable heavy launches a year
nodes.d: Fully reusable heavy launchers fly 300 or more orbital missions in one calendar year, three times the 100-flight milestone.

nodes.t: Starship internal cost under $300 per kg
nodes.d: SpaceX's internal cost to put a kilogram in low orbit on Starship falls below $300/kg, against about $1,500/kg on an optimized Falcon 9 Starlink flight and about $4,915/kg on expended Flight 14.

nodes.t: AI cuts new space hardware development cost by about 10-20%
nodes.d: Non-recurring development cost for new spacecraft and launch vehicles falls about 10-20% under the base case as engineering labor for analysis, design, software and verification shrinks; hardware, test articles and facilities do not shrink.

nodes.t: AI compute becomes Starship's second anchor customer
nodes.d: Orbital-compute satellites (SpaceX Starmind AI1 and peers) fill at least 10 Starship flights in one calendar year, so Starship cadence and production learning depend on AI compute demand as well as Starlink.

nodes.t: New satellite generations every year
nodes.d: Leading commercial constellation operators field a new satellite generation (new bus or payload, not only software) about every 12 months, against 18-36 months today.

nodes.t: Starship internal cost under $100 per kg
nodes.d: SpaceX's internal cost to put a kilogram in low orbit on Starship falls below $100/kg, a third of the $300/kg milestone.

nodes.t: Development cycles 20-30% shorter, not 10x
nodes.d: Development time (concept to launch) for new space systems started after AI adoption falls measurably.

nodes.t: Customers buy orbit under $1,000 per kg
nodes.d: Third-party customers can routinely buy dedicated heavy-lift launch below $1,000 per kilogram of customer payload delivered (not per kilogram of vehicle capacity), against a Falcon 9 dedicated median of about $5,300/kg and a rideshare floor of about $7,000/kg today.

nodes.t: A new reusable launcher from start to orbit in three years
nodes.d: A program in any country started in 2027 or later reaches orbit with a reusable medium or heavy launcher within three years of program start.

nodes.t: Leading firms halve development cycles
nodes.d: A leading firm completes a launch vehicle, crew or cargo vehicle, or new large spacecraft program, whose own pre-2027 comparable took 3 years or more, in at most half that time, with a published schedule analysis.

nodes.t: Engineering math posed as precise problems
nodes.d: Engineers and AI agents translate engineering questions (a stability margin, an error bound, whether a sensor layout determines a material property) into precise mathematical statements with explicit assumptions, ideally Lean-stated…

nodes.t: Chaos theorems in the release (weak link to orbits)
nodes.d: The openai/math families closest to orbital dynamics: positive metric entropy for the Chirikov standard map (146), counterexamples to strong forms of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture (347), sharp symplectic ball-packing criteria (343), and uniform limit-cycle bounds for planar polynomial vector fields (143).

nodes.t: How hard neural networks are to verify
nodes.d: A substantially complete complexity map for verifying the properties of neural networks used in perception and control (robustness, reachability, Lipschitz bounds), including which architectures or training regimes make verification tractable.

nodes.t: Classic radar-code problems settled (checked)
nodes.d: Two old problems behind radar pulse compression and spreading-code design, as claimed in the release.

nodes.t: Claimed limits of the workhorse quantum-chemistry method
nodes.d: Theorems marking where Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT), and any efficient universal method for electronic energies, must fail: some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation (278), the ground-state energy of continuum Coulomb systems is QMA-hard (275)…

nodes.t: Forced Navier–Stokes blowup independently checked
nodes.d: Outside experts run Comparator on the Lean proof and audit the statement of OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim that the forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations can blow up from smooth, finite-energy data.

nodes.t: Firmer math under elasticity, crack and inspection models
nodes.d: Independent confirmation of the release's elasticity and fracture results: smooth isotropic Lame moduli are uniquely determined by boundary measurements (372); metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, plus a conductivity nonuniqueness theorem from full boundary data (365)…

nodes.t: Hot spots conjecture (planar case) confirmed
nodes.d: Family 369 claims that on any simply connected planar domain, the slowest-decaying non-constant temperature mode of an insulated (Neumann) plate takes its maximum and minimum on the boundary, settling Rauch's 1974 conjecture for that class.

nodes.t: Faster solvers for building correct-by-design controllers
nodes.d: Family 104 claims quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games; its Lean part covers only a randomized algorithm for mean-payoff games.

nodes.t: Euler fluid equations proven to blow up in open space
nodes.d: A rigorous, likely computer-assisted, proof that the 3D incompressible Euler equations on R^3 with no boundary form a finite-time singularity from smooth, finite-energy data.

nodes.t: Boltzmann and Landau equations proven well-behaved
nodes.d: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness for the space-inhomogeneous Boltzmann and Landau equations with physical interactions (including Coulomb and very soft potentials), far from equilibrium.

nodes.t: Which plasma fluid models make mathematical sense
nodes.d: Ill-posedness and singularity results for Hall and electron MHD, ideal-MHD blowup inherited from Euler, and conditional regularity and continuation criteria for resistive MHD in 3D, the models used for space weather, magnetic nozzles and fusion-propulsion concepts.

nodes.t: Where fluid and kinetic models are not unique
nodes.d: A systematic set of nonuniqueness and ill-posedness results, with matching uniqueness criteria, for the Euler, Navier-Stokes, Boltzmann and MHD models engineers simulate.

nodes.t: Boltzmann foundations checked and scoped
nodes.d: Outside experts check and scope family 363 (Boltzmann solutions that conserve mass, momentum and energy exactly yet are non-unique) and family 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian hard-sphere gases, including fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan).

nodes.t: Clay rules on the forced Navier–Stokes breakdown claim
nodes.d: The Clay Mathematics Institute states whether OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 forced blowup result satisfies its official breakdown statements (C)/(D), which permit a smooth, decaying force.

nodes.t: AI answer on unforced Navier–Stokes passes outside checks
nodes.d: A proof of global smoothness for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (Clay statements A/B), or of finite-time blowup from smooth data with zero force, on R^3 or the torus.

nodes.t: Skolem and Positivity problems for linear loops settled
nodes.d: Decide whether a linear recurrence ever hits zero (Skolem) or always stays positive (Positivity), both open in general.

nodes.t: Turbulence laws proven
nodes.d: Theorems that 3D Navier-Stokes with natural forcing (smooth, generic or white-in-time) dissipates energy at a rate independent of viscosity (the 'zeroth law') and obeys Kolmogorov-type inertial-range scaling, in a well-posed statistical framework.

nodes.t: Clay recognizes an AI answer to unforced Navier–Stokes
nodes.d: The Clay Mathematics Institute states that an AI-produced proof settles the unforced 3D Navier–Stokes problem, either global smoothness (statements A/B) or blowup from smooth data with zero force, or changes its Millennium Problems listing to say so.

nodes.t: AI settles a Millennium problem other than Navier–Stokes
nodes.d: An AI-produced proof settles the Riemann hypothesis, the Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture or the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, either way, and passes outside checks (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance).

nodes.t: P vs NP resolved
nodes.d: Resolution of P vs NP, or of the barrier problems around it (superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits).

nodes.t: Guaranteed error bars for smooth-regime simulations
nodes.d: A posteriori estimators and computer-assisted methods that give guaranteed, not asymptotic, error bounds for nonlinear PDE solutions in smooth regimes: heat conduction, structures, laminar and steady flows, electrostatics.

nodes.t: Optimal control with proven guarantees
nodes.d: Existence, regularity and dimension-robust approximation theorems for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and reachability equations with state constraints, plus certified a posteriori error bounds for neural and tensor solvers, so guidance and collision-avoidance policies come with proofs.

nodes.t: How much sensor data is enough
nodes.d: Quantitative stability estimates, not just uniqueness, for the inverse problems behind structural health monitoring, heat-shield inspection, gravimetry and tomography: how measurement noise and sensor placement bound the damage or material properties that can be recovered.

nodes.t: Certified rare-event probabilities
nodes.d: Methods with provable, non-asymptotic error bounds for very small failure probabilities in high-dimensional, non-Gaussian models: 1e-4 collision probabilities, 1e-6 structural failure, margins.

nodes.t: Proven best designs for hard optimization problems
nodes.d: Moment-SOS, tight convex relaxations, branch-and-bound and MIP methods that certify a trajectory, layout or design is globally optimal, or within a proven gap, at engineering scale, using sparsity, symmetry and convergence-rate theory.

nodes.t: Radiation transport with error bounds
nodes.d: Deterministic and Monte Carlo radiation-transport methods (crew and electronics shielding, radiative heating during entry, neutronics for nuclear propulsion) with proven convergence and error bounds in the full 6+1-dimensional phase space, including asymptotic-preserving and low-rank solvers.

nodes.t: Quantum-chemistry shortcuts with certified error bars
nodes.d: Exchange-correlation functionals, learned or constructed, with statistically certified (conformal or Bayesian) error bars relative to a stated reference method (CCSD(T) or QMC) on defined chemical classes relevant to space (propellants, ablators, high-temperature alloys, electrolytes)…

nodes.t: Math expertise stops limiting space programs
nodes.d: The scarce resource in space-program analysis is no longer people who can do research-grade applied math.

nodes.t: Certified math on demand reaches the supplier base
nodes.d: Tier-2 and tier-3 space suppliers (structures, propulsion components, avionics boxes, thermal hardware) routinely produce analysis with AI-derived proofs, guaranteed error bars or certified rare-event bounds and deliver it in data packages to primes and operators.

nodes.t: A certifier audits AI analysis instead of redoing it
nodes.d: A certifying authority or mission-assurance office accepts AI-produced analysis with guaranteed bounds from verified numerics and independently checked derivations as certification evidence.

nodes.t: Formal astrodynamics library
nodes.d: Machine-checked definitions and core theorems for orbital mechanics (Kepler's equation, Lambert's problem, the circular restricted three-body problem and its Jacobi integral, Clohessy-Wiltshire relative motion, quaternion attitude kinematics, standard probability-of-collision definitions) in Lean or Isabelle…

nodes.t: Agents that prove real flight code
nodes.d: AI agents write contracts, loop invariants and proofs for production embedded code (C, Ada/SPARK, Rust) and discharge them in an existing checker (Frama-C, GNATprove, Verus, or Lean via extraction), at a marginal cost of compute hours instead of proof-engineer years.

nodes.t: Regulators accept AI-produced proofs
nodes.d: A certification authority or its delegate (an FAA ACO or DER under DO-178C with DO-333 and DO-330, a NASA center technical authority under NPR 7150.2, ESA product assurance under ECSS, or Space Force) accepts a software plan (PSAC or software development plan…

nodes.t: Landing-guidance solvers with proven convergence
nodes.d: Proofs of iteration bounds to stationarity, recursive feasibility and robustness margins for the real-time guidance formulations used in powered descent and proximity operations, lossless convexification for specific extended constraint classes, and robust or chance-constrained variants.

nodes.t: Machine-checked stability for guidance and control
nodes.d: Proofs that a guidance, control and estimation loop stays inside a safe envelope, including actuator saturation, sampling, delay, sensor gating and mode switches.

nodes.t: AI-drafted formal specifications
nodes.d: AI turns natural-language requirements, interface control documents and concepts of operations into formal, machine-checkable specifications (contracts, temporal logic, unit-typed interfaces).

nodes.t: Verified docking and capture logic
nodes.d: Reachability and barrier-certificate proofs for rendezvous, proximity operations, docking and debris capture that cover approach and abort trajectories, keep-out zones, mode switches, sensor dropouts and learned (neural) controllers under runtime assurance.

nodes.t: Adaptive control of flexible spacecraft, proven stable
nodes.d: Stability and performance proofs for adaptive and learning-augmented attitude, pointing and structural control of vehicles whose dynamics are poorly known before flight or change during it: large flexible arrays and radiators, close formation clusters, propellant slosh in large tanks…

nodes.t: Error-rate guarantees for onboard machine learning
nodes.d: Distribution-free and finite-sample guarantees for learned components that cannot be formally verified: conformal coverage and calibrated false-alarm and miss rates under stated distribution-shift models, sequential change-detection bounds, and sample-complexity bounds for online system identification.

nodes.t: Certified onboard trajectory optimizers
nodes.d: Embedded SOCP/QP solvers for powered-descent guidance, rendezvous MPC and collision avoidance with machine-checked proofs that, in the flight processor's floating-point arithmetic, they terminate within a fixed iteration budget and return an epsilon-feasible…

nodes.t: Guidance code with proven floating-point math
nodes.d: Machine-checked bounds on round-off, overflow and conversion errors for guidance, navigation, control and estimation code, generated per module by agents.

nodes.t: Verifying neural-network perception at flight scale
nodes.d: Proving robustness and correctness properties, over the operational domain, of neural networks used for terrain-relative navigation, hazard detection or pose estimation.

nodes.t: Validated limits on sensor and terrain behavior
nodes.d: Formally stated, test-validated envelopes for what sensors and environments can do during critical phases: laser rangefinder and altimeter dropouts and reflectivity, IMU saturation durations, terrain discontinuities, lighting.

nodes.t: AI red-teaming of flight assumptions
nodes.d: Agents search physics-based simulations and data for scenarios that break the assumptions under which flight software was proven or tested: terrain steps, saturation longer than designed, sensor delays, reboot timing, unit mismatches.

nodes.t: Exhaustive checks of fault logic and configuration
nodes.d: Agents build formal models of fault detection, isolation and recovery logic, mode machines, reboot and timing behavior, command sequences and parameter tables from code and interface documents.

nodes.t: Toolchain that ships guidance code with its proofs
nodes.d: An engineering pipeline in which engineers write formal requirements and AI agents produce guidance, navigation, attitude-control and collision-avoidance code together with machine-checked proofs of stability, constraint satisfaction and floating-point error bounds…

nodes.t: Proven safety wrappers for unverifiable autonomy
nodes.d: Instead of verifying a neural or learned controller, verify a small monitor, a recoverable-set (barrier) condition and a simple backup controller, and switch to the backup before safety is lost (the Simplex architecture).

nodes.t: Proven-correct guidance for entry and landing
nodes.d: Entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance (numerical predictor-corrector, convex powered-descent guidance) delivered with machine-checked proofs of convergence, constraint satisfaction and floating-point error bounds for the flight implementation, and accepted as verification evidence.

nodes.t: Formally verified engine control software
nodes.d: Machine-checked proofs that engine-controller and health-management logic (start sequencing, redlines, abort logic, numerical filters) meets its specification, produced by AI agents at low cost and accepted as verification evidence in a NASA human-rating or crewed-program review.

nodes.t: Lander flies proof-checked descent guidance and fault logic
nodes.d: A lunar lander flies terminal-descent GNC whose key properties are machine-checked, not only Monte Carlo-tested: altitude plausibility, measurement-rejection gates, engine-cutoff and reboot logic and the guidance law, plus, if the guidance uses an onboard optimizer, its convergence, feasibility and solver numerics.

nodes.t: Proof-checked autonomous docking, servicing and refueling
nodes.d: Rendezvous, proximity operations, docking, servicing or debris capture, and ship-to-ship propellant transfer flown with machine-checked passive safety (collision-free under failures), keep-out zones, abort reachability and capture logic, plus runtime assurance on the guidance, used as primary safety evidence.

nodes.t: Formally verified onboard software stack
nodes.d: Formally verified onboard software components fly on ordinary (non-research) missions: an seL4-class separation kernel or hypervisor, a telecommand parser, or software-update authentication; the first operational flight of any one of them counts.

nodes.t: A Mars lander flies proof-checked landing and fault logic
nodes.d: A lander reaches the surface of Mars flying entry, descent and landing guidance and fault-management logic whose key properties are machine-checked: sensor gating, mode switches, engine and reboot logic, and guidance numerics, with assumptions red-teamed against Mars atmosphere and terrain models.

nodes.t: Multicore space chip flies with proven worst-case timing
nodes.d: A radiation-tolerant multicore processor or SoC flies on an operational mission with machine-checked proofs that flight software keeps its worst-case timing whatever runs on the other cores, including an onboard AI payload.

nodes.t: Proof-backed guidance software in operational spacecraft
nodes.d: Operational uncrewed spacecraft (constellation satellites, landers, servicers) run GNC or collision-avoidance software whose safety case relies materially on AI-produced machine-checked proofs.

nodes.t: Proof-checked software updates across constellations
nodes.d: Each over-the-air update to thousands of satellites is gated by automatic re-proof of key invariants: collision-avoidance decision logic, safe-mode entry, deorbit command and decision logic, command authentication.

nodes.t: Reusable launchers re-prove flight software every flight
nodes.d: A reusable launch operator flies engine-control, redline, abort, fault-management and termination-interface logic whose key invariants are machine-checked, and re-proves them automatically on every software change between flights, and says so publicly.

nodes.t: Onboard AI agents fly under proof-checked command guards
nodes.d: An operational spacecraft (not a shadow-mode experiment) lets an unverified learned or language-model agent issue commands directly (tasking, health management, pointing, conjunction response, surface operations)…

nodes.t: Proof-backed autonomous flight termination under FAA rules
nodes.d: Autonomous flight safety system logic and other Part 450 computing-system safety items are licensed with formal proofs as an accepted means of compliance alongside RCC-319 testing.

nodes.t: Crewed lander autonomy certified with AI proofs
nodes.d: NASA human-rating (NPR 8705.2C with NPR 7150.2 Class A software), FAA commercial human-spaceflight rules or ECSS accept AI-produced machine-checked proofs as part of the certification evidence for crew-critical GNC autonomy (landing guidance, docking, abort and fault management).

nodes.t: Verified flight code 15-120x cheaper per line
nodes.d: The cost per functionally verified line (seL4-class full functional proof) falls from about $300-600 to roughly $5-20 under the base case, a 15-120x fall (central about 35-40x), because spec review dominates what remains and compute costs cents per line.

nodes.t: Assurance stops being a moat for primes
nodes.d: Small teams (lander and constellation startups) reach assurance levels that once required large verification departments, on uncrewed commercial and government work that needs no certification credit.

nodes.t: Verified autonomy becomes cheap
nodes.d: At early adopters the cost of verifying GNC and autonomy software falls by about half, making formally assured autonomy standard for smallsats and commercial landers rather than a NASA-only luxury.

nodes.t: Fewer missions lost to software logic (hard to see by 2031)
nodes.d: The share of mission losses caused by software logic, configuration and fault-management errors falls measurably.

nodes.t: Flight-software standards write in credit for AI proofs
nodes.d: A flight-software or assurance standard names AI-written, checker-verified proofs as an accepted verification method, so programs no longer argue the route plan by plan.

nodes.t: Flight-software verification takes half the calendar time
nodes.d: At a leading space firm, the calendar time to fully verify a safety-critical flight-software release, including proofs, hardware-in-the-loop runs and integrated vehicle regression, falls to half its 2026 level, and the firm, a customer or an agency review reports it.

nodes.t: AI agents audit cryptography at research grade
nodes.d: Frontier models run closed-loop cryptanalysis: they propose attacks on published schemes, protocols and parameter sets, test them, and return exact witnesses for a human to judge.

nodes.t: Optimal expander graphs for networks and codes (conditional)
nodes.d: 178 builds nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, the best possible spectral expanders, deterministically for every degree d>=3 and all large even sizes.

nodes.t: Hardness limits for scheduling and network planning (unaudited)
nodes.d: Hardness-of-approximation ceilings for the combinatorial problems behind constellation tasking, ground-station and gateway siting, routing, beam frequency assignment and network partitioning become formal claims awaiting outside checks rather than beliefs: beating Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut…

nodes.t: Capacity limits of laser and quantum links (conditional)
nodes.d: Proofs of the ultimate rates of the optical and quantum channels used for deep-space laser links, optical relays serving several receivers and satellite QKD: 273 (entropy photon-number inequality) makes the optical broadcast-channel capacity region and the thermal-noise optical wiretap secret-key capacity unconditional…

nodes.t: AI cracks post-quantum or space-link crypto (watch item)
nodes.d: Watch item, not a forecast: an AI-produced, independently verified cryptanalytic result that materially lowers the security of a standardized primitive used on satellite command and data links, above all ML-KEM/ML-DSA or the Module-LWE problems beneath them…

nodes.t: Near-optimal mesh routing with a proven gap
nodes.d: Joint optimization of laser-terminal pairing, routing and rate allocation over a time-expanded horizon that charges link acquisition and re-pointing time, at 10,000+ satellites, with a certified optimality gap (for example a Lagrangian dual bound) computed at operational cadence…

nodes.t: Proven error and spoofing bounds for satellite navigation
nodes.d: Provable integrity for Earth users who combine GNSS with low-orbit navigation signals, inertial sensors and signals of opportunity: error overbounds that hold for heavy-tailed, non-Gaussian and correlated errors…

nodes.t: AI lowers the quantum cost of breaking today's encryption
nodes.d: AI-designed quantum error-correcting codes (qLDPC and bivariate-bicycle families), logical instruction sets and arithmetic circuits lower the published spacetime cost (physical qubits x runtime) of Shor's algorithm for RSA-2048 or P-256 by at least 2x below the Oct-2026 best estimates for the same hardware assumptions…

nodes.t: Provable interference compliance for shared spectrum
nodes.d: Interference showings for NGSO-GSO and NGSO-NGSO sharing delivered as certified bounds instead of Monte Carlo runs: interval or proof-backed bounds on time-weighted throughput degradation, unavailability and aggregate EPFD, with the model assumptions written as a checkable specification.

nodes.t: Custom channel codes on request
nodes.d: AI designs codes and decoders for specific links, with machine-checked finite-blocklength performance claims.

nodes.t: Machine-checked security proofs for satellite quantum keys
nodes.d: Composable finite-key security proofs for satellite QKD passes (decoy-state BB84, BBM92, continuous-variable QKD) that include real device imperfections and non-IID signals.

nodes.t: Proven-correct post-quantum crypto for space processors
nodes.d: Agents produce implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HQC and hash-based signatures for space targets that have no verified library today (SPARC LEON, rad-hard RISC-V such as PIC64-HPSC and NOEL-V, FPGA fabric), with machine-checked functional correctness, constant-time and masking (side-channel) proofs…

nodes.t: Formally verified constellation routing software
nodes.d: Machine-checked proofs that routing, handover and topology-reconfiguration code is loop-free and deadlock-free, converges under link churn and meets latency bounds.

nodes.t: Certified availability for optical ground networks
nodes.d: Validated stochastic models of cloud, turbulence and pointing outage that predict the availability of a whole optical ground network with site diversity, with bounds good enough to sign service-level agreements against.

nodes.t: Receivers that beat photon counting
nodes.d: Theory and practical designs for joint-detection optical receivers that recover part of the gap between pulse-position modulation with photon counting and the Holevo limit, at deep-space photon flux and realistic background light.

nodes.t: Satellite antenna beams with proven emission limits
nodes.d: Beam weights, element-failure compensation and calibration for large satellite phased arrays (direct-to-device arrays, broadband user beams) computed with certified bounds: guaranteed peak-sidelobe and out-of-band power-flux limits over a stated array-error model…

nodes.t: Upgradeable satellite encryption with proven update paths
nodes.d: Spacecraft security designs that can change algorithms in orbit: hybrid classical plus post-quantum key exchange, hash-based signatures for commands and software, and a code-based fallback such as HQC.

nodes.t: Tasking and ground planning built on hardness limits
nodes.d: Tools for Earth-observation tasking, downlink scheduling, ground-station-as-a-service allocation and ground-station siting that combine exact solvers on structured instances, certified-gap heuristics and documented approximation ceilings, with AI formulating each mission's variant on request.

nodes.t: Constellation design with proven compliance
nodes.d: Design tools that co-optimize orbital shells, beam plans, spectrum use and laser topology, and output both a filing-ready design and certified interference and capacity bounds.

nodes.t: AI-designed photonics with proven performance bounds
nodes.d: AI-run inverse design of nanophotonic and flat-optics components for space (photonic-integrated couplers, filters and wavelength multiplexers for laser terminals; metasurface lenses and gratings for compact imagers and star trackers…

nodes.t: Multi-node satellite quantum-key demonstrations
nodes.d: Satellite QKD missions deliver keys among three or more ground nodes in different countries in routine campaigns: Eagle-1 in-orbit validation, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC and successors to China's Jinan-1.

nodes.t: Flight demo of verified post-quantum command links
nodes.d: A satellite flies post-quantum or hybrid authenticated telecommand and key exchange using machine-checked implementations, and performs an in-orbit algorithm swap.

nodes.t: Ground demo: optical receiver beats photon counting
nodes.d: A ground or lab demonstration in which a joint-detection receiver beats optimized PPM with photon counting by 25% or more in bits per received photon, at deep-space-like photon flux and background.

nodes.t: AI-designed codes ship in a satellite link standard
nodes.d: An AI-designed short-block code, decoder or synchronization scheme with machine-checked finite-blocklength claims is part of a published 3GPP non-terrestrial-network release or a CCSDS standard, and ships in handsets, modems or ground terminals.

nodes.t: Independent suppliers ship 3,000 laser terminals a year
nodes.d: Laser-terminal suppliers outside SpaceX, Amazon and China together deliver 3,000 or more space laser communication terminals in one year, so terminal supply no longer paces government, European or compute constellations.

nodes.t: Low-orbit navigation service with published error bounds
nodes.d: A low-Earth-orbit PNT service (Xona Pulsar, Iridium PNT, a European LEO-PNT follow-on, or a megaconstellation's navigation signal) publishes an integrity specification (alert limit, protection level, time to alert, fault rates) backed by derived overbounds, and paying critical users (telecom and power-grid timing…

nodes.t: Mega-constellation mesh run with certified optimality
nodes.d: A large LEO operator runs laser-mesh routing and radio resource allocation in production with certified per-snapshot optimality gaps and verified control-plane software.

nodes.t: Phone-to-satellite service scheduled around interference
nodes.d: Direct-to-device and broadband constellations schedule beams, power and emissions against certified interference budgets for adjacent bands, other operators and radio astronomy, instead of using blunt avoidance zones.

nodes.t: Weather-robust optical ground network service
nodes.d: An optical ground network sells weather-inclusive availability of about 99% for LEO or GEO data return, using site diversity, availability models and autonomous scheduling.

nodes.t: Satellite fleets can swap encryption before the 2035 cutoff
nodes.d: From this year, most new government and major commercial satellites carry in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto with machine-checked update paths, and legacy fleets are protected by ground-side controls.

nodes.t: Real-time spectrum sharing among rival constellations
nodes.d: Three or more NGSO operators in a shared band exchange ephemerides and beam plans and coordinate beams and power dynamically, under a protocol that carries machine-checked bounds on each party's throughput degradation (the FCC's 3% / 0.4% criteria) and proven convergence and fairness…

nodes.t: Certified quantum-key service from space
nodes.d: An accredited European or allied satellite QKD service (for example the EuroQCI space segment) routinely delivers keys to government users across 10 or more ground nodes, with a security evaluation that accepts its finite-key proof.

nodes.t: Constellation designed with certified tools enters service
nodes.d: A new constellation shell or satellite generation whose orbits, beam plan, spectrum use and laser topology came from a design optimizer with certified interference and capacity bounds (comms-constellation-design-optimizer) is built, launched and in commercial service, and its coordination showings carry those bounds.

nodes.t: Deep-space laser ground station gets more bits per photon
nodes.d: An operational optical ground station receiving from a deep-space or far-cislunar laser terminal uses a joint-detection receiver and returns more bits per received photon than optimized pulse-position modulation with photon counting, under live conditions.

nodes.t: Software adds 10%+ capacity on the same hardware
nodes.d: AI-produced mathematics and software (certified optimization, coexistence scheduling, custom codes) raise a major constellation's usable capacity by at least 10% at fixed hardware and spectrum, compared with the same hardware run with 2026-era software, disclosed by the operator or measured independently.

nodes.t: Machine-checked crypto becomes a procurement norm
nodes.d: Government space buyers (for example SDA, or ESA for IRIS²) require machine-checked implementation and protocol proofs for the security functions of new satellites.

nodes.t: International shift to provable spectrum sharing
nodes.d: The ITU follows the FCC in replacing fixed EPFD limits with performance-based sharing criteria and checkable compliance showings.

nodes.t: Satellites in service switch to post-quantum encryption
nodes.d: At least one operator of long-lived satellites (GEO, MEO or a government constellation) switches the key exchange and command authentication of several operational satellites from RSA or elliptic-curve algorithms to post-quantum or hybrid algorithms in orbit…

nodes.t: Code-breaking quantum computer exists
nodes.d: A quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 or 256-bit elliptic-curve keys exists.

nodes.t: Aviation approves low-orbit navigation with proven integrity
nodes.d: An aviation authority (FAA or EASA) or an ICAO standard accepts a LEO navigation service, alone or combined with GNSS, for an operation that needs integrity, for example through an RTCA or EUROCAE avionics standard, resting on the provider's published integrity overbounds and fault statistics.

nodes.t: Regulators review with AI tools
nodes.d: The FAA's Office of Commercial Space Transportation, the FCC, NASA safety boards and ESA reviewers use AI systems to re-run and check applicants' flight-safety analyses, environmental documents and safety cases, raising reviewer throughput 2-5x without changing the rules.

nodes.t: AI-ready structural and thermal test data
nodes.d: Machine-readable databases of the physical evidence this domain runs on: shell-buckling tests with measured imperfections, fatigue and crack-growth spectra, thermal-vacuum correlation sets, microgravity two-phase flow data and deployment telemetry, opened to AI models inside agencies and large firms.

nodes.t: Tests chosen for information, not habit
nodes.d: AI designs development test campaigns, the tests operators control, with Bayesian optimal experimental design and sequential testing, choosing which tests, levels, sensors and replicates buy the most margin knowledge.

nodes.t: Launch range and airspace scheduled by optimizer
nodes.d: Range (Eastern, Western, Starbase) and national-airspace scheduling for hundreds to thousands of launches and reentries a year is done by optimization tools that minimize hazard-area closures and conflicts, so range time stops being a cadence limit.

nodes.t: Structural margins with certified uncertainty bounds
nodes.d: Reliability-based structural margins with rigorous rare-event probability estimates and quantified model-form error, as a defensible alternative to stacked deterministic factors (ultimate factors of ~1.25-1.4, model-uncertainty factors, test factors).

nodes.t: Damage detection with proven detection limits
nodes.d: Problem-specific stability estimates, optimal sensor placement and model-assisted probability of detection (MAPoD) for guided-wave, strain and electrical-resistance damage sensing, telling engineers what damage size a given sensor layout can and cannot see.

nodes.t: Worst-case imperfection theory for thin shells
nodes.d: Rigorous answers to the open question of which manufacturing imperfections (shape, amplitude, number, location) most reduce the buckling load of thin cylinders and cones, with provable lower bounds on the knockdown factor given a factory's measured imperfection statistics.

nodes.t: Material strength limits from far fewer test samples
nodes.d: Statistical methods with proven coverage (hierarchical Bayesian, ICME-informed, transfer learning across machines and lots) that yield A- and B-basis design allowables from far fewer physical tests, accepted in MMPDS Volume II, CMH-17 and NASA-STD-6030 practice.

nodes.t: Certified bridges from microstructure to part properties
nodes.d: Quantitative homogenization and coarse-graining theorems with computable error bounds for nonlinear, inelastic, random microstructures (printed metals, ceramic-matrix composites), so effective properties and their scatter follow from microstructure statistics with certified error.

nodes.t: A rulebook for trusting AI-made analysis
nodes.d: NASA-STD-7009, ECSS and Space Force test standards, or a faster NASA handbook, interim or engineering directive, or ECSS handbook, gain a defined way to count AI-generated analyses (with independently checked derivations, quantified model error and, where available, certified numerics) as verification evidence…

nodes.t: Closing the mid-frequency vibration gap
nodes.d: Error-controlled prediction of launch vibroacoustic response in the mid-frequency band (roughly a few hundred Hz to ~1-2 kHz), where finite-element models are too costly and statistical energy analysis is invalid, via hybrid FE-SEA and reduced-order models with a posteriori error bounds.

nodes.t: Finite-element solvers with machine-checked error bounds
nodes.d: Structural and thermal finite-element solvers (linear statics, modal, steady conduction-radiation) whose discretization and floating-point errors carry proved bounds (guaranteed a posteriori estimators plus verified arithmetic), so an analysis result ships with a certificate.

nodes.t: Predictive physics of 3D-printed metal parts
nodes.d: Validated process-structure-property models for laser powder-bed fusion and directed-energy deposition that predict porosity, microstructure, residual stress and fatigue scatter from process parameters and in-situ sensor signals, with quantified uncertainty.

nodes.t: Predictive damage and fatigue models for reusable structures
nodes.d: Validated physics-based models of crack growth and composite damage progression under the low-cycle, high-amplitude, cryogenic and thermal-cycling spectra of reusable stages and tanks, replacing conservative empirical scatter factors and knockdowns.

nodes.t: License analyses drafted and checked by AI
nodes.d: AI agents produce and cross-check the Part 450 flight-safety analysis (debris, far-field overpressure, toxic release, expected casualty), the ground-safety analysis and the NEPA environmental documents that operators submit, turning months of specialist effort into days.

nodes.t: Anomaly diagnosis 3-10x faster
nodes.d: AI agents do the cognitive part of anomaly investigations (telemetry forensics, fault-tree pruning, physics re-simulation of candidate causes, corrective-action analysis), so return to flight is set by hardware fixes and verification tests rather than diagnosis.

nodes.t: AI agents run and check structural and thermal analysis
nodes.d: AI agents set up, run, check and document finite-element stress, loads, buckling and thermal analyses end to end (meshing, boundary conditions, margins of safety, thermal-model correlation to thermal-vacuum data, coupled-loads cycles), with an engineer signing off.

nodes.t: Test stands that run themselves
nodes.d: Engine stands, thermal-vacuum chambers, vibration tables and materials rigs run around the clock under AI control with adaptive test sequences and automatic data reduction, cutting test-to-insight time from weeks to hours and raising utilization where scheduling, not demand or article supply…

nodes.t: Satellites screened by statistics, not unit tests
nodes.d: For lines building hundreds to thousands of satellites a year, acceptance screening (unit-level vibration, thermal cycling, burn-in) is set by models that combine process data, sampled testing and early-life fleet telemetry, with a certified bound on the rate of defective units that escape to orbit.

nodes.t: Insurance-grade models of launch and in-orbit risk
nodes.d: Risk models that insurers, brokers and operators' own risk-retention programs can price on: hierarchical reliability for launchers with few flights (borrowing strength across vehicles and subsystems with honest uncertainty), in-orbit failure rates with heavy tails and early-life effects…

nodes.t: Lighter buckling design rules for tanks and interstages
nodes.d: Probabilistic or mechanistic knockdown factors tied to measured imperfection statistics, beyond NASA SP-8007-2020's deterministic analysis-based approach, become routine agency and industry practice for cylinders and cones, including composite shells where a blanket 0.65 is still common.

nodes.t: Certify each printed part from its build data
nodes.d: In-situ monitoring plus a validated physics/ML digital twin certifies each printed part ('print and fly') with reduced CT and witness testing, accepted first for non-fracture-critical and then for fracture-critical spaceflight hardware.

nodes.t: Models cut the test flights needed to prove reliability
nodes.d: Launch and spacecraft certifiers (Space Force NSSL new-entrant certification, NASA Launch Services Program risk categories, human-rating boards, or component reliability demonstrations) accept AI-produced, credibility-graded physics and flight-data models as Bayesian priors in reliability demonstration…

nodes.t: Qualification by analysis replaces some structural tests
nodes.d: Agencies (NASA, ESA, Space Force) accept AI-produced, uncertainty-quantified analysis in place of a strength qualification test beyond what NASA-STD-5001B already allows: for composite or bonded primary structure, or for metallic structure at tested-hardware factors of safety instead of the larger no-test factors.

nodes.t: Tighter launch vibration and acoustic environments
nodes.d: Component and spacecraft random-vibration, acoustic and shock test levels set with a reduced qualification margin over a model-predicted maximum predicted environment (MPE), from error-bounded predictions calibrated on early flight data, for new vehicles where flight data are sparse…

nodes.t: Analysis replaces some environmental qualification tests
nodes.d: NASA, Space Force and ESA mission-assurance practice grants formal test credit to validated, AI-produced analysis for derivative hardware in structures and thermal: reduced or deleted vibration, acoustic or thermal qualification tests (or levels) on derivative units…

nodes.t: Operators fly new hardware qualified mainly by AI analysis
nodes.d: A commercial operator or bus vendor that carries its own risk (no regulator, insurer or government customer accepts the evidence) flies a new-design, not heritage-derived, spacecraft subsystem or structure whose qualification rests mainly on AI-produced analysis with stated uncertainty plus development tests and accept…

nodes.t: Sensor-based inspection credit for reusable stages
nodes.d: Built-in structural health monitoring with quantified probability of detection replaces scheduled teardown or scanning inspection for defined zones of reusable stages or tanks between flights.

nodes.t: First flight structure sized with AI-certified margins
nodes.d: A launch-vehicle barrel, interstage or large spacecraft primary structure flies after being sized with AI-derived knockdowns tied to measured imperfection statistics and certified uncertainty margins, beyond SP-8007-2020's analysis-based approach, at 10-30% lower mass for its buckling-critical parts.

nodes.t: Test standards write in credit for AI analysis
nodes.d: A base revision of a structural or environmental test standard (NASA-STD-5001, GSFC-STD-7000 GEVS, SMC-S-016, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 or ECSS-E-ST-32-10) states when credibility-graded, AI-produced analysis may reduce or replace a qualification test, and with what factors and evidence.

nodes.t: Launch licensing in weeks
nodes.d: Routine license modifications (new trajectory, cadence or payload class) clear in under 30 days, new vehicle operator licenses in under 90 days from a complete application (against the 180-day statutory maximum), and FCC satellite approvals in months.

nodes.t: Sensors and models track wear on reusable stages
nodes.d: Fully reusable heavy launchers (Starship-class and peers) manage structural life with validated life models (data-driven or physics-based) and built-in sensors, sustaining fast turnaround without routine teardown inspection and with life limits set by analysis rather than fleet-leader experience alone.

nodes.t: New government designs fly qualified mostly by analysis
nodes.d: A NASA Class C or D mission, a Space Development Agency tranche or an ESA mission flies a new-design spacecraft structure or subsystem with no flight heritage whose qualification rests mainly on AI-produced, credibility-graded analysis plus development tests and acceptance-level workmanship screening.

nodes.t: Crewed vehicle structure certified with fewer strength tests
nodes.d: A NASA human-rating or crewed-program certification (crew vehicle, lander, pressurized rover or station module) accepts AI-produced, credibility-graded analysis in place of at least one planned static-strength or ultimate-load qualification test of primary structure, at standard factors of safety.

nodes.t: Structures and thermal analysis cycles 2-5x faster
nodes.d: Time from a requirement change to signed-off stress, loads and thermal analysis (not design-build-test) compresses 2-5x across the industry, cutting non-recurring engineering and allowing more design iterations per program.

nodes.t: New space materials reach flight in five years or less
nodes.d: Concept-to-flight insertion of new space materials (alloys, TPS, PV) takes five years or less, shown by at least three material programs started in 2027 or later that each fly within five years of start.

nodes.t: Qualification campaigns at least 15% shorter
nodes.d: Typical qualification campaigns for derivative spacecraft and launch-vehicle subsystems on programs started in 2028 or later run at least 15% shorter than the pre-2027 baseline of roughly 12-24 months (about 10-20% in the base case and 20-30% in Recursive, per the physical-gate table…

nodes.t: Model-priced insurance for new rockets and constellations
nodes.d: Insurance capacity extends to risks the market now avoids or prices on scant history: launch cover for a new reusable vehicle after only a few flights at rates near those of mature vehicles, or in-orbit and correlated-loss (space-weather or debris) cover for a LEO constellation, written on model-based rating.

nodes.t: 5-15% lighter structures on new vehicles and spacecraft
nodes.d: Vehicles and spacecraft designed from ~2028 show 5-15% lower structural mass for equivalent loads, spacecraft first and launch-vehicle primary structure later.

nodes.t: Qualification campaigns 30% shorter at leading firms
nodes.d: At leading space firms, qualification campaigns for spacecraft and launch-vehicle subsystems on programs started in 2031 or later run at least 30% shorter than the pre-2027 environmental qualification baseline of roughly 6-18 months.

nodes.t: How chaotic systems respond to design changes
nodes.d: Theorems that long-time averages of chaotic systems (turbulent flows, plasma turbulence, the thermosphere) depend differentiably on design parameters, with computable bounds and convergent algorithms.

nodes.t: Reliable automated structure identification
nodes.d: Robust, uncertainty-aware solution of the characterization inverse problem (automated Rietveld refinement, disorder-aware phase identification, fusion of X-ray, neutron and electron-microscopy data) so autonomous labs' claims of new materials survive expert scrutiny.

nodes.t: Combustion chemistry simulated with certified error
nodes.d: Error theory, reduced kinetic mechanisms and verified structure-preserving stiff ODE/DAE integrators for large reaction networks (combustion, ablation, plasma chemistry, batteries), with provable error bounds on ignition delay, heat release and key species that hold for non-dissipative chemistry.

nodes.t: Atomistic AI models with trustworthy error bars
nodes.d: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) that report calibrated, property-level uncertainty (melting point, diffusion barrier, elastic constants) with documented coverage on held-out chemistries (formal coverage only under stated distribution-shift assumptions) and out-of-distribution flags…

nodes.t: Certified combustion-stability models
nodes.d: Low-order acoustic-network or Galerkin models of chamber thermoacoustics, delivered with rigorous linear and nonlinear stability margins: Lyapunov or sum-of-squares certificates and bounds on Hopf bifurcation and triggering amplitude under an uncertain flame-response band.

nodes.t: Automated checks that engine flow simulations are right
nodes.d: AI agents run code verification (manufactured solutions), solution verification (grid and time-step refinement; adjoint or a-posteriori error estimates for steady and RANS cases), uncertainty quantification and NASA-STD-7009-style credibility assessment on every propulsion simulation at near-zero marginal labor.

nodes.t: Limits on measuring propellant in low gravity
nodes.d: Proofs of which tank-fill states can be identified in microgravity from boundary sensors (capacitance, radio-frequency or impedance-type tomography), plus gauging algorithms with guaranteed error bounds.

nodes.t: Error bars for turbulent and shocked flows
nodes.d: Rigorous statistical error bounds for simulations of chaotic, turbulent and shock-laden flows (combustors, plumes, reentry wakes): a proven framework (for example statistical or measure-valued solutions) that states which LES/DNS statistics converge under mesh refinement…

nodes.t: Chemical accuracy from cheap quantum chemistry
nodes.d: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals and atomistic models trained on wavefunction-level data that reach about 1 kcal/mol accuracy at semi-local DFT cost, extended from main-group molecules to transition metals, oxides and solids.

nodes.t: Long-life predictions from short tests
nodes.d: Mechanism-based models with validated uncertainty that predict 10,000-hour creep rupture, oxidation and thermomechanical fatigue of high-temperature alloys and coatings from roughly 1,000-hour tests.

nodes.t: Validated models of cryogenic propellant in microgravity
nodes.d: Predictive models of self-pressurization, slosh, line chilldown and tank-to-tank transfer in low gravity, validated on flight data with quantified uncertainty (tank pressure within ~5%, boil-off within ~10%).

nodes.t: Predictive theory of detonation-engine wave modes
nodes.d: A validated model of how many detonation waves an RDRE runs, when it switches modes, and how injectors couple to the waves, as functions of flow rate, mixture and back-pressure, so that engines can be designed to hold one stable mode.

nodes.t: Turbulence and combustion models with guarantees
nodes.d: AI-built RANS, LES subgrid and flamelet closures that are realizable, frame-invariant and consistent in known limits, carry generalization bounds, and are validated across separated, swirling and reacting benchmark classes without per-case tuning.

nodes.t: Predictive flame response at engine pressures
nodes.d: First-principles prediction of injector flame transfer functions and transcritical real-fluid mixing for LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 at 100-350 bar.

nodes.t: Quantum computers beat classical chemistry
nodes.d: A fault-tolerant quantum computation delivers a chemically accurate result for an industrially relevant molecule or material that the best classical methods (DMRG, AFQMC, coupled cluster, neural wavefunctions) cannot match.

nodes.t: AI-generated engines at scale
nodes.d: Computational engineering models generate complete additively-manufactured engines (geometry, regenerative cooling, injectors) in weeks.

nodes.t: AI-designed green and high-energy propellants
nodes.d: Multi-objective molecular and formulation design of propellants that jointly predicts performance (specific impulse, density), sensitivity, thermal stability, toxicity and synthesizability, closing the loop with automated small-scale synthesis.

nodes.t: AI designs new rocket-engine alloys in weeks
nodes.d: AI agents run the full integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) loop (composition, phase stability, printability, heat treatment, predicted creep, oxidation and hydrogen resistance) for printed high-temperature alloys, with a high hit rate on first validation coupons.

nodes.t: Probabilistic engine life prediction for reuse
nodes.d: Physics-based life models for thermomechanical fatigue, low-cycle fatigue and creep in chambers, turbines and additively-manufactured parts, with uncertainty quantification, updated after each flight from sensors and inspection.

nodes.t: Predictive engine start and relight transients
nodes.d: Validated system-level models of line chilldown, ignition, turbopump spin-up and combustion onset for in-flight relights after a coast, used to design start sequences with quantified margin.

nodes.t: Predictive turbopump cavitation and stability
nodes.d: Models that predict rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability for new inducer and pump designs before water-flow and hot-fire tests.

nodes.t: Gradient design of turbulent and chaotic systems
nodes.d: Design tools that compute reliable sensitivities of time-averaged quantities in unsteady turbulent or plasma flows (combustor stability margins, nozzle heat loads, thruster erosion), enabling gradient optimization over thousands of parameters instead of sampling.

nodes.t: Design out combustion instability before hot fire
nodes.d: An integrated workflow (predicted flame response, a certified reduced-order stability model and uncertainty quantification) that ranks injector and chamber designs by stability margin before hardware is built, used on a real engine program.

nodes.t: Ship-to-ship cryogenic transfer demonstrated
nodes.d: Two Starships dock in low Earth orbit and transfer tens to 100+ tonnes of LOX and liquid methane, with measured boil-off, chilldown loss and transfer efficiency.

nodes.t: Public flight data on storing cryogenic propellant in orbit
nodes.d: NASA and Eta Space's LOXSAT (Electron launch, nine months in LEO) completes its liquid-oxygen demonstration of zero-loss storage, high-accuracy gauging, automated pressure control and transfer, and NASA publishes comparisons of its predictive models against the flight data.

nodes.t: Autonomous labs discover real new materials
nodes.d: AI-run labs deliver independently replicated new functional materials (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes, catalysts, alloys) at more than ten times the human discovery rate.

nodes.t: Detonation engine flies in space
nodes.d: A rotating detonation rocket engine of about 1,000 lbf or more operates as primary propulsion in a space or lander flight demonstration, beyond suborbital hops.

nodes.t: First AI-agent-designed alloy flies in a rocket engine
nodes.d: An alloy proposed by an agentic AI/ICME design loop after 2027 (materials-ht-alloy-design) flies in flight hardware (combustion chamber, preburner, turbine or nozzle, including a small thruster or kick-stage part) on a commercial launch vehicle or spacecraft.

nodes.t: AI-designed propellant flies
nodes.d: A propellant molecule or formulation primarily proposed by an AI design system is qualified and flown in a spacecraft or launch-vehicle propulsion system.

nodes.t: Full lunar-lander refueling campaign
nodes.d: Roughly 10-20 tanker flights fill a depot in LEO, which transfers a full load to Starship HLS for a lunar landing (uncrewed demo or crewed).

nodes.t: Model-based engine reuse life
nodes.d: Reusable engines whose overhaul and inspection intervals are set by validated probabilistic life models, extending the flights between overhauls (for example 2x) without added risk.

nodes.t: Detonation engines in operational service
nodes.d: RDREs used as production propulsion on a commercial lander, upper stage or in-space vehicle, with predictable, qualified behavior.

nodes.t: Longer-life reusable engines from new alloys
nodes.d: Operational reusable engines whose hot-section parts (preburners, turbines, chambers) use AI-designed alloys and model-backed life prediction, extending refurbishment intervals or allowing higher chamber pressure.

nodes.t: An engine built around an AI-designed alloy flies
nodes.d: A new rocket engine or major engine version flies with hot-section parts (preburner, turbine, chamber or nozzle) made from an alloy proposed by an AI design loop, and the alloy is what lets it run a hotter preburner or turbine, or a higher chamber pressure, than its heritage alloys allow.

nodes.t: One lunar lander makes three landings, refueled in space
nodes.d: One lunar lander is refueled beyond low Earth orbit (in lunar orbit, near-rectilinear halo orbit or on the surface) and makes at least three landings on the Moon, reusing its engines and tanks between them.

nodes.t: Routine orbital refueling economy
nodes.d: Depots and tankers operate routinely, with dozens of cryogenic transfers per year supporting lunar landers, Mars ships and high-energy missions, and boil-off and transfer losses are predicted rather than padded.
